topics.name: Isaiah: overview
topics.description: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
evidence: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?

topics.name: The Lord charges his rebellious children
topics.description: The LORD calls heaven and earth to witness that the children he raised have rebelled, rejects their empty sacrifices, and offers cleansing if they are willing and obedient.
evidence: Retell the charge of Isaiah 1:2-4
Explain why God rejects the sacrifices in 1:11-15 and what he asks instead in 1:16-17
Quote the offer in 1:18-20
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he is weary of sacrifices in Isaiah 1 and what he commands instead?

topics.name: The mountain of the Lord in the last days
topics.description: Isaiah sees the mountain of the LORD's house raised up, nations streaming to learn his ways, and weapons turned into farming tools; the house of Jacob is called to walk in his light.
evidence: Describe what the nations say and do in Isaiah 2:2-4
Explain the image of swords into plowshares from the text
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what Isaiah 2:2-4 says will happen to the nations and to weapons in the last days?

topics.name: The day of the Lord humbles the proud
topics.description: Judah is full of silver, horses and idols, and a day of the LORD is coming on everything lofty so that he alone is exalted and men are told to cease trusting in man.
evidence: List what Judah is full of in Isaiah 2:7-8
Say what the day of the LORD comes against (2:12-17)
Explain the command in 2:22
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the day of the LORD brings against the proud in Isaiah 2:12-17?

topics.name: Jerusalem stripped of support
topics.description: The Lord takes away Jerusalem's leaders and supplies, the people oppress one another, the elders and the proud daughters of Zion are charged, and the city is left desolate.
evidence: Name the supports taken away in Isaiah 3:1-3
Describe the LORD's charge against the elders in 3:14-15
Describe the fate of the haughty daughters of Zion (3:16-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD takes from Jerusalem in Isaiah 3 and why?

topics.name: The Branch of the Lord and the cleansed remnant
topics.description: After judgment, the Branch of the LORD is beautiful and glorious, those left in Zion are called holy, and the LORD covers Zion with cloud by day and fire by night as a shelter.
evidence: Say who is called holy in Isaiah 4:3
Describe the cloud, fire and shelter over Zion in 4:5-6
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD does for Zion in Isaiah 4:2-6 after washing away her filth?

topics.name: The song of the vineyard
topics.description: Isaiah sings of a beloved's well-tended vineyard that yields wild grapes, and the LORD explains that the vineyard is the house of Israel, for which he looked for justice and righteousness.
evidence: Retell what the owner did for the vineyard (5:1-2)
Say what he will do to it (5:5-6)
Explain who the vineyard is according to 5:7
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the song of the vineyard and say what Isaiah 5:7 says it means?

topics.name: Six woes and the distant nation
topics.description: Isaiah pronounces woes on land-grabbers, drunkards, those who call evil good and those who pervert justice, and says the LORD will summon a swift nation from afar against his people.
evidence: List the woes of Isaiah 5:8, 11, 18, 20, 21 and 22
Explain why the LORD's anger is not turned away (5:24-25)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name at least three of the woes in Isaiah 5 and the reason given for judgment in 5:24?

topics.name: Isaiah sees the Lord and is sent
topics.description: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the LORD enthroned with seraphim crying holy, is cleansed by a coal from the altar, volunteers, and is told to preach to a people who will not understand until a stump remains.
evidence: Retell what the seraphim say and do (6:2-7)
Explain Isaiah's response in 6:5 and 6:8
Describe the message he is given and the "holy seed" in 6:9-13
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell Isaiah's vision in chapter 6, including what the seraphim cry and how Isaiah is cleansed?

topics.name: The sign of Immanuel to Ahaz
topics.description: When Syria and Ephraim threaten Judah, Isaiah tells Ahaz to trust the LORD, Ahaz refuses to ask a sign, and the Lord gives a sign of a son called Immanuel, with Assyria coming on the land.
evidence: Explain what Rezin and Pekah plan against Judah (7:1-6)
Quote the sign in 7:14 and say to whom the word is addressed (7:13)
Describe the coming of the king of Assyria (7:17-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the setting of Isaiah 7:14 and what Ahaz was told to do in 7:4-9?

topics.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz and the Assyrian flood
topics.description: Isaiah writes a name-sign for a son, the LORD warns that the king of Assyria will flood Judah, tells Isaiah not to fear what the people fear, and calls him to the law and testimony instead of mediums.
evidence: Explain the meaning of the child's name sign in 8:1-4
Say whom Isaiah is told to fear and sanctify (8:12-13)
Explain the contrast between the law and testimony and consulting the dead (8:19-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says to sanctify him rather than fear what the people fear in Isaiah 8:11-13?

topics.name: Light for the people in darkness and the child born
topics.description: Light shines on the people in darkness in Zebulun and Naphtali, the yoke is broken, and a child is born whose government, names and everlasting reign are on the throne of David.
evidence: Name the regions mentioned in Isaiah 9:1
List the names given to the child in 9:6
Explain what 9:7 says about his throne and kingdom
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 9:6-7 says about the child and the throne of David?

topics.name: His hand is stretched out still
topics.description: A refrain runs through four stanzas: Ephraim's pride, unrepentant people, false leaders and civil strife bring judgment, and the LORD's anger is not turned away; woe is also pronounced on unjust decrees.
evidence: Find the repeated refrain in Isaiah 9:12, 17, 21 and 10:4
Say what Ephraim's boast in 9:10 shows about the people's attitude
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} find the refrain repeated in Isaiah 9:8-10:4 and explain why the people are judged?

topics.name: Assyria the rod, then judged
topics.description: The LORD sends Assyria as the rod of his anger against a hypocritical nation, but punishes the king of Assyria for his boasting; a remnant will return and Zion is told not to fear.
evidence: Explain how Assyria is both used and judged (10:5-7, 12-15)
Say what is promised to the remnant (10:20-23)
Describe the comfort given to Zion in 10:24-27
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the axe boasting against the one who swings it in Isaiah 10:15?

topics.name: The shoot from the stem of Jesse
topics.description: A shoot from Jesse's stem, endowed with the Spirit of the LORD, judges the poor with righteousness; peace reaches even the animals, the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD, and the remnant is gathered.
evidence: List the gifts of the Spirit resting on him in Isaiah 11:2
Describe how he judges (11:3-5)
Describe the peaceful creation in 11:6-9 and the gathering in 11:10-12
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the one who comes from the stem of Jesse and the peace of his kingdom in Isaiah 11?

topics.name: A song of salvation
topics.description: In that day the redeemed will praise the LORD, saying God is their salvation and strength, draw water from the wells of salvation, and call all the earth to sing.
evidence: Quote the declaration of trust in Isaiah 12:2
Say what the people are told to do in 12:4-6
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the people sing in Isaiah 12 and why they can praise the LORD?

topics.name: The burden of Babylon and the fallen king
topics.description: The LORD musters an army against Babylon, a day of the LORD brings desolation by the Medes, and a taunt song mocks the king of Babylon who said he would ascend and be like the Most High.
evidence: Name the people the LORD stirs up against Babylon (13:17)
Describe the king's boast and his fall in 14:12-15
Say what mercy the LORD shows Jacob in 14:1-3
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the proverb against the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14:4-20?

topics.name: The LORD's purpose against Assyria and Philistia
topics.description: The LORD swears to break Assyria on his mountains, declares his purpose stretched over all nations, and tells Philistia not to rejoice, since Zion is founded by the LORD.
evidence: Say what the LORD has sworn about Assyria (14:24-25)
Quote the answer to the messengers in 14:32
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says in Isaiah 14:24-27 about his purpose?

topics.name: The burden of Moab
topics.description: Moab is laid waste in a night and mourns, a request is made for Moab's outcasts to find shelter in Judah where a throne is established in mercy, and Moab's pride is judged with a time limit.
evidence: Describe the mourning of Moab (15:2-5)
Say what is said of the throne in 16:5
Identify the time limit given in 16:14
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Isaiah 15-16 portrays Moab's fall and the grief it causes?

topics.name: Damascus, Israel and the land beyond Ethiopia
topics.description: Damascus becomes a ruin and Ephraim's fortress ceases, a remnant turns to its Maker, and the roaring nations are rebuked; Ethiopia is addressed and a gift is brought to the LORD at Zion.
evidence: Say why Ephraim is judged according to Isaiah 17:10
Describe the fate of the roaring nations (17:12-14)
Say what happens to Ethiopia's people in 18:7
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the burden of Damascus and the reason given in Isaiah 17:10?

topics.name: The burden of Egypt and Isaiah's sign
topics.description: The LORD comes against Egypt, whose counsel fails; yet he promises that Egypt will know and serve him, and that Egypt, Assyria and Israel will be a blessing; Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign against trusting Egypt and Ethiopia.
evidence: Describe the judgment on Egypt (19:1-15)
Describe the blessing on Egypt, Assyria and Israel (19:23-25)
Explain what Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot signifies (20:2-6)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Isaiah 19:19-25 says will happen to Egypt and what Isaiah's sign in chapter 20 means?

topics.name: Babylon's fall, Dumah and Arabia
topics.description: Isaiah watches in fear at a grievous vision, the watchman announces that Babylon is fallen, Seir asks the watchman what remains of the night, and Arabia's glory is to fail within a year.
evidence: Describe what the watchman reports in Isaiah 21:6-9
Say what the watchman answers in 21:11-12
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the watchman's report in Isaiah 21:6-9?

topics.name: The valley of vision and Shebna
topics.description: Jerusalem is distressed by a day of trouble; the people prepare defenses but do not look to the LORD and say let us eat and drink; Shebna is removed and Eliakim receives the key of the house of David.
evidence: Say what the people do and fail to do in Isaiah 22:8-13
Explain what happens to Shebna and Eliakim (22:15-25)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jerusalem does in Isaiah 22:8-13 and what the LORD says about it?

topics.name: The burden of Tyre
topics.description: Tyre, the merchant city, is laid waste by the LORD's purpose, forgotten seventy years, and afterward returns to her trade, which will be holy to the LORD.
evidence: Say who purposed Tyre's fall and why (23:9)
Describe what happens after seventy years (23:15-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 23 says about Tyre's fall and her trade after seventy years?

topics.name: The LORD lays waste the earth
topics.description: The LORD empties the earth because its people broke the laws and the everlasting covenant; joy ceases, the earth reels, the host on high and kings below are punished, and the LORD reigns in Zion.
evidence: Say why the earth is defiled (24:5)
Describe the punishment of the host on high and the kings of the earth (24:21-22)
Say where the LORD reigns (24:23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the earth is emptied in Isaiah 24 and who reigns at the end?

topics.name: A feast on the mountain and death swallowed up
topics.description: The LORD makes a feast for all peoples on his mountain, removes the veil over all nations, swallows up death, wipes away tears, and the redeemed say they waited for him.
evidence: Describe the feast and the veil (25:6-7)
Quote what the LORD does to death and tears (25:8)
Say what the people say in 25:9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for all peoples on his mountain in Isaiah 25:6-9?

topics.name: A song in Judah: perfect peace and the dead who live
topics.description: Judah sings of a strong city and perfect peace for those who trust the LORD, laments that they have brought no deliverance, and hears that the LORD's dead shall live and the earth will disclose her slain.
evidence: Quote the promise of peace in Isaiah 26:3
Say what is promised about the dead in 26:19
Describe the call to hide until the indignation is past (26:20-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 26:3 and 26:19 promise?

topics.name: Leviathan punished and the vineyard of red wine
topics.description: The LORD punishes leviathan, the vineyard he guards will fill the world with fruit, Jacob's iniquity is purged, and the scattered are gathered with a great trumpet to worship at Jerusalem.
evidence: Say what the LORD does to leviathan (27:1)
Describe the vineyard and its keeper (27:2-6)
Describe the gathering in 27:12-13
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the vineyard of Isaiah 27 and compare it with the vineyard in Isaiah 5?

topics.name: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
topics.description: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
evidence: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?

topics.name: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
topics.description: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
evidence: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?

topics.name: Rebellious children and trust in Egypt
topics.description: Judah sends to Egypt for help instead of asking the LORD, refuses to hear true prophecy, and is told that in returning and rest is salvation; the LORD will wait to be gracious and will beat down Assyria.
evidence: Say why the LORD calls the people rebellious (30:1-2, 9-11)
Quote 30:15 and the people's answer in 30:16
Describe the grace promised in 30:18-26
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the people were told in Isaiah 30:15 and how they answered?

topics.name: Woe to those who trust in horses
topics.description: Those who go to Egypt for help trust in chariots rather than the LORD, who is wise and will protect Jerusalem like birds flying; Assyria will fall by a sword not of man.
evidence: Say what the people trust instead of the LORD (31:1)
Quote the contrast in 31:3
Describe how the LORD defends Jerusalem (31:4-5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast Egypt's horses with the LORD's help in Isaiah 31:1-3?

topics.name: A king reigns in righteousness; the Spirit is poured out
topics.description: A king and princes will reign in righteousness, careless women are warned of coming desolation, until the Spirit is poured from on high and righteousness and peace dwell in the land.
evidence: Describe the king and the changes in 32:1-8
Say what ends the desolation (32:15)
Say what the work of righteousness is (32:17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what 32:15-17 says happens when the Spirit is poured out?

topics.name: The destroyer destroyed and the LORD our king
topics.description: The spoiler is warned, the people pray for grace, the LORD rises to be exalted, sinners in Zion fear the devouring fire, and the righteous see the king; the LORD is judge, lawgiver and king.
evidence: Say who asks, "Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire?" and the answer (33:14-16)
Quote 33:22
Describe Jerusalem as a quiet habitation (33:20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say the three roles given to the LORD in Isaiah 33:22?

topics.name: The day of vengeance on the nations and Edom
topics.description: The LORD's indignation is on all nations; his sword comes down on Edom for the controversy of Zion, and the land becomes a lasting wasteland inhabited by wild creatures.
evidence: Say what the LORD does to the host of heaven and the nations (34:2-4)
Say which land receives the sword (34:5-6)
Describe Edom after judgment (34:9-15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Edom is singled out in Isaiah 34:5-8?

topics.name: The desert blooms and the way of holiness
topics.description: The wilderness blossoms, the weak are strengthened, the blind see and the lame leap, and a highway of holiness leads the ransomed to Zion with everlasting joy.
evidence: Describe the healings in Isaiah 35:5-6
Say who walks the way of holiness (35:8-10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the way of holiness and the people who walk it in Isaiah 35?

topics.name: Sennacherib's envoy mocks Jerusalem
topics.description: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year Sennacherib's envoy Rabshakeh stands by Jerusalem's conduit and tries to turn the people from trusting Hezekiah and the LORD.
evidence: Retell the arguments Rabshakeh uses (36:4-10, 14-20)
Say how Hezekiah's officers respond (36:21-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what Rabshakeh says to Jerusalem's people in Isaiah 36 and how they answer?

topics.name: Hezekiah prays and the angel strikes the Assyrian camp
topics.description: Hezekiah takes the letter to the LORD's house and prays; Isaiah answers that the LORD will defend Jerusalem, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp so that Sennacherib returns to Nineveh.
evidence: Retell Hezekiah's prayer (37:14-20)
Say what Isaiah's answer promises (37:21-35)
Retell what happens to Sennacherib (37:36-38)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah's prayer in Isaiah 37?

topics.name: Hezekiah's sickness and recovery
topics.description: Hezekiah, told he will die, prays and weeps; the LORD adds fifteen years, promises to deliver the city from Assyria, and gives a sign with the shadow on the sundial; Hezekiah writes a thanksgiving.
evidence: Retell what Isaiah first says to Hezekiah and how Hezekiah responds (38:1-3)
Say what the LORD adds and the sign given (38:5-8)
Describe the lesson of the writing in 38:17-20
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah when he was sick in Isaiah 38?

topics.name: Envoys from Babylon
topics.description: Merodach-baladan sends letters to Hezekiah, who shows them all his treasures; Isaiah tells him everything will be carried to Babylon, and Hezekiah calls the word good because there will be peace in his days.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah shows the envoys (39:2)
Say what Isaiah foretells (39:5-7)
Describe Hezekiah's response (39:8)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah told Hezekiah about Babylon and how Hezekiah answered?

topics.name: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
topics.description: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
evidence: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?

topics.name: The LORD chose Israel; idols have no answer
topics.description: The LORD calls Israel his servant, the seed of Abraham his friend, and tells them not to fear; he challenges the idols to declare the future and raises up one from the north and east.
evidence: Quote the promise in Isaiah 41:10
Say how Israel is addressed in 41:8-14
Describe the challenge to the idols (41:21-29)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Israel in Isaiah 41:8-10 and how he challenges the idols?

topics.name: Behold my servant
topics.description: The LORD presents his chosen servant, on whom he puts his Spirit, who brings justice to the nations gently and is given as a covenant and a light to the Gentiles to open blind eyes.
evidence: List what the LORD says of the servant (42:1-4)
Say what the servant is given for (42:6-7)
Explain 42:8 about the LORD's glory
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the servant and his work in Isaiah 42:1-7?

topics.name: A new song and the blind servant
topics.description: The LORD is called to be praised to the ends of the earth and goes forth as a warrior, but his servant is blind and deaf; Jacob was given to plunder because they would not walk in his ways.
evidence: Describe the new song and the LORD as a warrior (42:10-13)
Explain what is said of the blind and deaf servant (42:18-20)
Say why Jacob was given to spoil (42:24-25)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD calls his servant blind and deaf in Isaiah 42:18-25?

topics.name: I have redeemed you; I am the LORD, your Saviour
topics.description: The LORD redeems and calls Jacob by name, will be with them through waters and fire, gathers sons from the ends of the earth, calls Israel his witnesses, does a new thing, and blots out their transgressions for his own sake.
evidence: Quote the promise in Isaiah 43:1-2
Say what Israel is called in 43:10-12
Explain the "new thing" (43:18-19) and the forgiveness in 43:25
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Isaiah 43:1-2 and 43:25?

topics.name: The folly of idols and the Spirit poured out
topics.description: The LORD pours his Spirit on Jacob's seed and declares he is first and last with no God beside him, while the idol-maker's craft is shown to be foolish; the LORD blots out transgressions.
evidence: Quote 44:6
Describe how the idol is made and used (44:12-17)
Say what the LORD says to Israel in 44:21-22
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Isaiah 44:9-20 calls idol-making foolish?

topics.name: Cyrus, the LORD's shepherd and anointed
topics.description: The LORD names Cyrus, by name before his time, as his shepherd and anointed who will let Jerusalem and the temple be rebuilt, so that all will know there is none else.
evidence: Say what the LORD says of Cyrus (44:28, 45:1)
Explain why the LORD calls Cyrus by name (45:4-6)
Quote the invitation in 45:22-23
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says Cyrus will do and why in Isaiah 44:28-45:6?

topics.name: Babylon's gods carried, Israel carried by God
topics.description: Bel and Nebo are carried off as burdens while the LORD has carried Israel from birth and to old age; he declares the end from the beginning.
evidence: Contrast who carries whom in Isaiah 46:1-4
Say what the LORD declares in 46:9-10
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast the gods of Babylon with the LORD in Isaiah 46:1-4?

topics.name: The fall of Babylon the lady of kingdoms
topics.description: The virgin daughter of Babylon is brought down from her throne, for she showed the LORD's people no mercy and trusted in sorceries and in saying "I am, and none else"; her counsellors cannot save her.
evidence: Say why Babylon is judged (47:6-8)
Describe what her sorceries and astrologers cannot do (47:12-15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Babylon is brought low in Isaiah 47?

topics.name: The obstinate house of Jacob and the furnace of affliction
topics.description: The LORD tells Jacob he foretold things because they were obstinate, delays his anger for his name's sake, calls them out of Babylon, and says had they heeded his commandments their peace would be like a river.
evidence: Say why the LORD declared things beforehand (48:3-7)
Describe the call to leave Babylon (48:20-21)
Quote 48:22
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he tested Israel in the furnace of affliction in Isaiah 48:10-11?

topics.name: The servant, a light to the nations
topics.description: The servant called from the womb, whose mouth is like a sharp sword, says he has laboured in vain; the LORD says it is too light a thing to restore Israel and gives him as a light to the Gentiles, and promises Zion she is not forgotten.
evidence: Describe how the servant is called (49:1-3)
Quote the LORD's answer in 49:6
Say what the LORD says to Zion in 49:14-16
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says is "too light a thing" for his servant in Isaiah 49:6?

topics.name: The servant who gives his back to the smiters
topics.description: The servant says the Lord GOD opened his ear and he was not rebellious, gave his back to those who struck him, and sets his face like flint trusting the Lord's help; those who walk in darkness are urged to trust the LORD.
evidence: Describe what the servant endures (50:5-6)
Say why he is not ashamed (50:7-9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what the servant says he will endure and why he is not put to shame in Isaiah 50:4-9?

topics.name: Awake, arm of the LORD
topics.description: Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah, the LORD promises comfort and a law going forth, the arm of the LORD is called to awake as in ancient days, and Jerusalem is told the cup of fury is taken from her.
evidence: Say whom they are told to look to (51:1-2)
Describe the cry to the arm of the LORD (51:9-11)
Say what happens to the cup of trembling (51:22-23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who the people are told to look to in Isaiah 51:1-2 and why?

topics.name: Awake, Zion: good tidings of peace
topics.description: Jerusalem is told to put on strength, she is redeemed without money, the feet of the one who brings good tidings are beautiful, and the LORD has bared his arm before the nations.
evidence: Quote 52:7
Say what the watchmen see (52:8)
Describe the command to depart in 52:11-12
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what 52:7 describes about the one who brings good tidings?

topics.name: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
topics.description: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
evidence: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?

topics.name: Sing, barren one: the covenant of peace
topics.description: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, the LORD her husband has called her back with mercy, swears as with the waters of Noah, and promises a covenant of peace that will not be removed.
evidence: Describe the call to the barren woman (54:1-3)
Say what the LORD compares his oath to (54:9)
Quote the promise in 54:10
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD compares his promise in Isaiah 54:9-10 to the waters of Noah?

topics.name: Come, buy without money: the sure mercies of David
topics.description: The LORD invites the thirsty to come without money, promises an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, calls the wicked to return, and says his word will accomplish what he pleases.
evidence: Quote the invitation in Isaiah 55:1-3
Say what is promised to those who return (55:7)
Explain 55:10-11
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who is invited and what is promised in Isaiah 55:1-7?

topics.name: Foreigners and eunuchs welcomed; blind watchmen
topics.description: The LORD says foreigners and eunuchs who hold to his covenant and keep sabbaths will be joyful in his house of prayer for all peoples, while blind watchmen and greedy shepherds are condemned.
evidence: Say who is welcomed in Isaiah 56:3-7

topics.description: An escapee tells Ezekiel in the twelfth year of captivity that the city has been struck down, and Ezekiel's mouth is opened; the LORD rebukes those in the ruined land who claim it, and the exiles who hear Ezekiel as a pleasant song without doing his words.

topics.description: The LORD condemns shepherds who feed themselves and scatter his flock, promises to seek and gather his sheep himself, to judge between the fat and lean, and to set one shepherd, his servant David, over them with a covenant of peace.

topics.name: The mountains of Israel will bear fruit again
topics.description: The LORD speaks to the mountains of Israel, which the nations have mocked, promising that his people will return, cities be rebuilt, the land be fruitful, and the land no longer devour men or bear the nations' reproach.

topics.name: I will sprinkle clean water and give a new heart and spirit
topics.description: The LORD says he will act for his holy name, not Israel's sake: he will gather them, sprinkle clean water on them, give a new heart and put his Spirit within them so they keep his statutes, and make the land like Eden.

topics.description: The Spirit sets Ezekiel in a valley of very dry bones and asks if they can live; as Ezekiel prophesies, bones, sinews, flesh and breath come into them as an exceeding great army, which the LORD says is the whole house of Israel he will raise from their graves.

topics.description: Ezekiel joins two sticks marked for Judah and for Joseph to show the LORD will make them one nation under one king, David his servant, with a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant, and his sanctuary among them for evermore.

topics.name: Gog of Magog comes against Israel
topics.description: The LORD sets himself against Gog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, who with many allies will come from the north in the latter years against Israel dwelling safely, and the LORD brings him with earthquake, sword, pestilence and fire so that nations know he is the LORD.

topics.name: Gog defeated and Israel restored
topics.description: Gog and his army fall on the mountains of Israel, weapons are burned for seven years and the dead buried over seven months, birds and beasts feast, and the LORD says he will bring back the captivity of Jacob and pour out his Spirit on Israel.

topics.name: The vision of the temple: the man with the measuring reed
topics.description: In the twenty-fifth year of the exile Ezekiel is taken in visions of God to a high mountain in Israel and led by a man with a line and measuring reed through the gates and courts of a new temple complex, with tables for sacrifices and chambers for priests.

topics.name: The temple house, its chambers and the walled area
topics.description: The man measures the temple house with its side chambers, panelling carved with cherubim and palm trees, the priests' holy chambers, and the outer wall around the whole to separate the holy from the common.

Say who may and may not minister (44:9-16)

Quote the command to the princes (45:9-10)
Say what the prince provides at the feasts (45:17-25)

Say what the prince may not do (46:18)
Describe the kitchens (46:19-24)

topics.name: The river flowing from the temple
topics.description: Water flows from under the threshold of the temple and grows from ankle-deep to a river that cannot be crossed, flows east into the Dead Sea healing its waters, and trees on its banks bear fruit every month with leaves for healing.

Say what happens where the river goes (47:8-9)
Describe the trees (47:12)

topics.description: The LORD gives the borders of the land to be divided among the twelve tribes by lot, with strangers who live among them also receiving inheritance in the tribe where they live.

Say what is said of strangers (47:22-23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Ezekiel 47:22-23 says about foreigners living among Israel?

topics.description: The land is divided into parallel portions for the twelve tribes with a central holy district for priests, Levites, city and prince; the city has twelve gates named for the tribes and its name from that day is The LORD is there.

Name the city's gates (48:31-34)

topics.name: Daniel: overview
topics.description: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, serve under Babylonian and Persian kings, and are delivered in the furnace and lions' den; Daniel interprets dreams and receives visions of kingdoms, the Ancient of days, and the end.

Say which kings Daniel served (1:21, 5:31, 6:28)
Describe the two halves of the book: stories (1-6) and visions (7-12)

topics.name: Daniel and his friends refuse the king's food
topics.description: Taken to Babylon and chosen for training, Daniel determines not to defile himself with the king's food and wine; after a ten-day trial of vegetables and water they look healthier, and God gives the four young men knowledge and wisdom.

Describe the ten-day test (1:11-16)
Say what God gave the four young men (1:17)

topics.name: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great image
topics.description: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him his forgotten dream; Daniel and his friends seek God, who reveals the dream of an image of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay struck by a stone that becomes a mountain, which Daniel interprets as kingdoms and God's kingdom that will never be destroyed.
evidence: Describe the image and the stone (2:31-35)
Say what Daniel says of God in 2:20-22 and 2:28
Report Daniel's interpretation of the parts and the stone (2:37-45)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the dream of the image and say what Daniel says the stone represents in Daniel 2:44-45?

topics.name: The fiery furnace
topics.description: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and orders everyone to worship it; Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse, are thrown into a blazing furnace, and are seen walking unharmed with a fourth figure, so the king praises their God.
evidence: Retell the king's command and the three men's answer (3:4-6, 16-18)
Describe what the king sees in the furnace (3:24-25)
Say how the king responds (3:28-30)

topics.name: Nebuchadnezzar's tree and his humbling
topics.description: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree cut down, Daniel interprets it as the king being driven from men until he knows the Most High rules, and the king, proud of Babylon, loses his reason for seven times and then praises the King of heaven.
evidence: Describe the dream (4:10-17)
Say what Daniel advises the king (4:27)
Retell what happens to Nebuchadnezzar and how it ends (4:30-37)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of Nebuchadnezzar's great tree and say what he learned in Daniel 4:34-37?

topics.name: The writing on the wall
topics.description: At Belshazzar's feast, where the temple vessels are used to praise idols, fingers write on the wall; Daniel reads MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN as the numbering, weighing and dividing of the kingdom, and that night Belshazzar is slain.
evidence: Describe the feast and the writing (5:1-5)
Say what Daniel reminds Belshazzar of (5:18-23)
Report the meaning of the writing and what happens (5:25-31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what appeared at Belshazzar's feast and what Daniel said it meant in Daniel 5?

topics.name: Daniel in the lions' den
topics.description: Under King Darius, officials who cannot find fault with Daniel secure a decree against prayer to anyone but the king; Daniel keeps praying to God toward Jerusalem, is thrown to the lions, and is found unharmed in the morning because God shut their mouths.
evidence: Retell why the officials plot against Daniel (6:4-9)
Describe how Daniel prays and what happens (6:10-23)
Say what Darius decrees at the end (6:25-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of Daniel in the lions' den and say why he was thrown there in Daniel 6?

topics.name: Four beasts and the Ancient of days
topics.description: In Belshazzar's first year Daniel dreams of four beasts rising from the sea, the last with ten horns and a boastful little horn; thrones are set, the Ancient of days sits in judgment, the beast is slain, and one like a son of man is given an everlasting kingdom.

Describe the Ancient of days and the judgment (7:9-12)
Describe the one like the Son of man and what he is given (7:13-14)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the four beasts, the Ancient of days and the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:1-14?

topics.name: The vision of the beasts interpreted
topics.description: An attendant tells Daniel the four beasts are four kings, the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom for ever, and the little horn wars against the saints and speaks against the Most High until judgment is given and the kingdom is given to the saints.
evidence: Say what the beasts and horns are told to be (7:17, 23-24)
Describe what the little horn does (7:21, 25)
Say what happens to the saints and the kingdom (7:18, 22, 26-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Daniel is told the beasts are and what happens to the saints in Daniel 7:15-27?

topics.name: The ram, the goat and the little horn
topics.description: In the third year of Belshazzar Daniel sees a two-horned ram defeated by a goat with a great horn, which is broken into four, and a little horn that attacks the sanctuary and the daily sacrifice; Gabriel explains the ram as Media and Persia and the goat as Greece.
evidence: Describe the ram, goat and horns (8:3-12)
Report what Gabriel says the ram and goat are (8:20-21)
Say what length of time is given until the sanctuary is cleansed (8:13-14) and how Daniel responds (8:27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the ram and the goat in Daniel 8 and what Gabriel says they are?

topics.name: Daniel's prayer of confession
topics.description: Reading in Jeremiah that Jerusalem's desolation would last seventy years, Daniel prays with fasting, confessing that Israel has sinned and not heeded the prophets, that the curse written in the law of Moses has come, and asks God to act for his own name's sake.
evidence: Say what Daniel understood from the books (9:2)
List elements of his confession (9:5-14)
Say on what ground he asks God to hear (9:16-19)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what prompted Daniel's prayer in Daniel 9:2 and what he confesses?

topics.name: Gabriel and the seventy weeks
topics.description: While Daniel prays, Gabriel comes to give him understanding: seventy weeks are determined for his people and the holy city to finish transgression and bring in everlasting righteousness, with the Messiah the Prince, a city rebuilt, a Messiah cut off, and a desolation.
evidence: Say when Gabriel comes and why (9:20-23)
List what the seventy weeks are for (9:24)
Report what is said of the Messiah the Prince and of the city and the sanctuary (9:25-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel says the seventy weeks are for in Daniel 9:24?

topics.name: A vision of a man clothed in linen
topics.description: In the third year of Cyrus Daniel mourns three weeks and, by the river Hiddekel, sees a man in linen with a radiant appearance whose voice leaves him without strength; he is strengthened, told his words were heard, and that a struggle with the prince of Persia involved Michael.
evidence: Describe the man Daniel sees (10:5-6)
Say how Daniel responds and is strengthened (10:7-19)
Say what the messenger says of the prince of Persia and Michael (10:12-13, 20-21)

topics.name: Kings of the south and the north
topics.description: The messenger tells Daniel of Persian kings, a mighty king whose kingdom is divided to the four winds, and a long series of conflicts between kings of the south and north including alliance by marriage, wars and a raiser of taxes.

Describe the rivalry between the king of the south and the king of the north (11:5-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the pattern of conflict between the kings of the south and north in Daniel 11:5-20?

topics.description: A vile person gains a kingdom by flatteries, turns against the holy covenant, takes away the daily sacrifice and sets up the abomination of desolation; the wise instruct many and some fall; a king exalts himself above every god until his end.

Say what happens to the people who know their God (11:32-35) and to the king in 11:36-45

topics.name: Michael stands up; many shall awake
topics.description: Michael stands up in a time of trouble, those written in the book are delivered, many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, the wise shine like stars, and Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end and go his way to rest.

Say what Daniel is told to do with the book (12:4, 9)
Report what Daniel is told for himself (12:13)
